title: Flattened 830 Square Miles 💥
hook_sentence: On the morning of 30 June 1908 at around 7:14 local time, near the Podkamennaya Tunguska River in Central Siberia, a cataclysm struck .
narration_script: On the morning of 30 June 1908 at around 7:14 local time, near the Podkamennaya Tunguska River in Central Siberia, a cataclysm struck . By one estimate, the blast devastated more than 830 square miles (2,150 square km) of taiga forest, flattening trees in a distinctive radial pattern. Scientists calculate the airburst released between 10 and 15 megatons of TNT. Atmospheric pressure waves generated by the explosion rippled across the globe and were detected by barographs worldwide. Scientific consensus attributes the event to an atmospheric meteor air burst, though no celestial fragment has ever been formally identified from that sudden Siberian morning.
closing_sentence: Scientific consensus attributes the event to an atmospheric meteor air burst, though no celestial fragment has ever been formally identified from that sudden Siberian morning.
caption:
A Siberian forest vanished under a blinding blast. 💥

Near the Podkamennaya Tunguska River in Central Siberia, physical models suggest the incoming celestial body measured roughly 160 to 200 feet (50 to 60 meters) across. Wood samples from surviving trees near the epicenter revealed deformed tracheid cells and light rings in 1908, followed by 4 to 5 years of suppressed growth. Scientists calculate the airburst released between 10 and 15 megatons of TNT without leaving behind an identified cosmic fragment.

Could modern civilization withstand a silent cosmic airburst over an urban center today? 🌌
